title: Superposition of Waves
subject: Physics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: What is the Principle of Superposition of Waves?
cards.a: When two or more wave pulses arrive simultaneously at a point in a medium, each wave produces its own displacement independently, and the resultant displacement is the vector sum of individual displacements: y = y₁ + y₂.
cards.hint: Applies strictly to linear media where wave speed is independent of amplitude.

cards.q: Phase change on reflection of transverse/longitudinal waves at a Rigid vs Free boundary?
cards.a:
Rigid (denser) boundary: Phase change of π radians (180°), path change of λ/2. Crest reflects as trough (compression reflects as compression).
Free (rarer) boundary: Phase change of ZERO radians (0°). Crest reflects as crest.
cards.hint: Rigid boundary exerts an equal and opposite reaction force, inverting the phase by 180°.

cards.q: Equation of a Stationary (Standing) Wave on a stretched string?
cards.a: y = [ 2 A cos(k x) ] · sin(ω t) = R sin(ω t), where resultant amplitude is R = 2 A cos(k x) = 2 A cos(2π x / λ).
cards.hint: Formed by superposition of two identical waves traveling in opposite directions. There is zero net transfer of energy!

cards.q: Nodes vs Antinodes: Definitions and spacing?
cards.a:
Nodes (N): Points where amplitude is MINIMUM (zero), strain is maximum. Positions: x = (2p + 1) λ / 4.
Antinodes (A): Points where amplitude is MAXIMUM (2A), strain is zero. Positions: x = p λ / 2.
Distance between consecutive N-N or A-A: λ / 2.
Distance between consecutive N-A: λ / 4.
cards.hint: All particles between two consecutive nodes vibrate in the same phase with varying amplitudes.

cards.q: Velocity of a transverse wave along a stretched string of tension T and linear density m?
cards.a: v = √(T / m) = √[ T / (π r² ρ) ], where m = M/L = π r² ρ is mass per unit length.
cards.hint: Increasing tension increases speed; using thicker/denser wire decreases speed.

cards.q: Fundamental frequency of a stretched string vibrating between two fixed ends?
cards.hint: String vibrates in one loop (L = λ/2 ⇒ λ = 2L) with nodes at both ends and an antinode at center.

cards.q: Harmonics and Overtones of a vibrating string fixed at both ends?
cards.a:
ALL harmonics are present in integer ratios: n₁ : n₂ : n₃ : ... = 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 : ...
Fundamental / 1st Harmonic: n
1st Overtone / 2nd Harmonic: n₁ = 2 n
2nd Overtone / 3rd Harmonic: n₂ = 3 n
p-th Overtone: n_p = (p + 1) n.
cards.hint: p-th overtone has (p + 1) loops, (p + 2) nodes, and (p + 1) antinodes.

cards.q: State the Three Laws of Vibrating Strings.
cards.a:
1. Law of Length: n ∝ 1/L (n L = const, if T and m are constant).
2. Law of Tension: n ∝ √T (n / √T = const, if L and m are constant).
3. Law of Linear Density: n ∝ 1/√m (n √m = const, if L and T are constant).
cards.hint: Verified experimentally using a Sonometer.

cards.q: Fundamental frequency of an air column in a Pipe CLOSED at one end?
cards.a: n_c = v / (4 L), where v is speed of sound in air and L is length of pipe.
cards.hint: Closed end is always a NODE; open end is always an ANTINODE (L = λ/4 ⇒ λ = 4L).

cards.q: Harmonics in a Pipe CLOSED at one end: Which are present?
cards.a:
ONLY ODD harmonics are present! Ratio: n : n₁ : n₂ : ... = 1 : 3 : 5 : 7 : ...
Fundamental / 1st harmonic: n_c = v / (4L)
1st overtone / 3rd harmonic: n₁ = 3 n_c
2nd overtone / 5th harmonic: n₂ = 5 n_c
p-th overtone = (2p + 1)-th harmonic: n_p = (2p + 1) n_c.
cards.hint: Even harmonics are completely absent in a pipe closed at one end!

cards.q: Fundamental frequency of an air column in a Pipe OPEN at both ends?
cards.hint: Both ends are ANTINODES (L = λ/2 ⇒ λ = 2L). Note: n_o = 2 × n_c for identical lengths!

cards.q: Harmonics in a Pipe OPEN at both ends: Which are present?
cards.a:
ALL harmonics (both even and odd) are present! Ratio: 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 : ...
Fundamental / 1st harmonic: n_o = v / (2L)
1st overtone / 2nd harmonic: n₁ = 2 n_o
2nd overtone / 3rd harmonic: n₂ = 3 n_o
p-th overtone = (p + 1)-th harmonic: n_p = (p + 1) n_o.
cards.hint: Sound from an open pipe is richer and more musical than a closed pipe because all harmonics are present.

cards.q: What is End Correction (e) for open and closed pipes?
cards.a:
Antinode at open end forms slightly outside the boundary at distance e = 0.3 d, where d is internal diameter.
Pipe closed at one end: L' = L + e = L + 0.3 d
Pipe open at both ends: L' = L + 2 e = L + 0.6 d.
cards.hint: Open pipe has TWO open ends, so end correction is 2e = 0.6d!

cards.q: Resonance Tube Experiment: Formula for End Correction and Speed of Sound v?
cards.a:
For first and second resonance lengths l₁ and l₂:
End correction: e = (l₂ - 3 l₁) / 2
Speed of sound: v = 2 n (l₂ - l₁).
cards.hint: Taking difference (l₂ - l₁) eliminates the unknown end correction e completely!

cards.q: What is the phenomenon of Beats?
cards.a:
Periodic variation in intensity of sound (waxing and waning) produced by the superposition of two sound waves of slightly different frequencies traveling along the same path.
Beat frequency: n_b = |n₁ - n₂|.
cards.hint: Period of beats: T_b = 1 / |n₁ - n₂|. Human ear can distinguish beats only if n_b ≤ 10 Hz (persistence of hearing = 0.1 s).

cards.q: Tuning Fork frequency alteration: Loading with wax vs Filing prongs?
cards.a:
Loading with wax: Increases mass/inertia ⇒ Frequency DECREASES (n ↓).
Filing the prongs: Decreases mass ⇒ Frequency INCREASES (n ↑).
cards.hint: Board & CET favorite! Use n_new = n_known ± n_b to determine unknown frequency before and after wax loading.

cards.q: Relation between frequency of a stretched wire and its diameter d and density ρ?
cards.hint: Doubling the diameter halves the fundamental frequency if tension and length remain constant.

cards.q: Stationary waves vs Progressive waves: Energy transfer and particle amplitude?
cards.a:
Progressive: Waves travel forward, transfer energy and momentum, all particles vibrate with SAME amplitude.
Stationary: Waves do not advance, ZERO net energy transfer, particles vibrate with DIFFERENT amplitudes (0 at nodes, 2A at antinodes).
cards.hint: In stationary waves, energy is trapped between nodes.

cards.q: Intensity I of a sound wave: Dependencies on amplitude A and frequency n?
cards.a:
I = 2 π² ρ v n² A² ⇒ I ∝ n² and I ∝ A².
Loudness in decibels: β = 10 log₁₀(I / I₀), where reference intensity I₀ = 10⁻¹² W/m² (threshold of hearing).
cards.hint: Doubling amplitude quadruples intensity (I' = 4 I).

cards.q: If an open pipe of length L is dipped vertically in water up to half its length, what is the new fundamental frequency?
cards.a:
New frequency n' = n (the original fundamental frequency)!
Originally open pipe: n = v / (2L). Dipping halfway forms a closed pipe of length L/2: n' = v / [ 4(L/2) ] = v / (2L) = n.
cards.hint: Clever MHT-CET trap! Halving length and closing one end cancel each other out.

cards.q: General Doppler Effect formula for sound?
cards.a: Apparent frequency: n' = n · [ (v ± v_L) / (v ∓ v_S) ], where v is speed of sound, v_L is listener speed, v_S is source speed.
cards.hint: Upper signs for approach (frequency increases); lower signs for recede (frequency decreases).

cards.q: Does Doppler Effect occur when source and observer move in same direction with same speed?
cards.a: NO. If relative velocity between source and observer is zero (v_L = v_S in same direction), apparent frequency equals actual frequency (n' = n).
cards.hint: Doppler shift requires NON-ZERO relative motion along the line joining source and listener.

cards.q: Musical Sound Characteristics: Pitch, Loudness, and Quality (Timbre)?
cards.a:
Pitch: Depends on Frequency (high frequency = sharp/shrill; low frequency = grave/flat).
Loudness: Depends on Intensity and Amplitude² (subjective sensation on ear).
Quality (Timbre): Depends on number, order, and relative amplitudes of overtones (harmonics).
cards.hint: Quality allows distinguishing between notes of same pitch and loudness played on different instruments (e.g. violin vs flute).

cards.q: Sonometer wire: Frequency change when tension T is increased by x% (small change)?
cards.a:
Since n ∝ √T: Δn / n ≈ (1/2) (ΔT / T).
If tension increases by 2%, frequency increases by ≈ 1%.
cards.hint: Fractional change in frequency is half the fractional change in tension.

cards.q: MHT-CET Trap: A wave is represented by y = 0.05 sin(100π t - 2π x). What is the wave speed?
cards.a:
v = ω / k = (100π) / (2π) = 50 m/s in positive x-direction.
Frequency n = ω / 2π = 50 Hz; wavelength λ = 2π / k = 1 m.
cards.hint: Never confuse wave speed v = ω/k with particle maximum velocity v_p,max = ω A = 100π × 0.05 = 5π m/s!
